Four congruent semicircles are inscribed in a square of side length \(1\) so that their diameters are on the sides of the square, one endpoint of each diameter is at a vertex of the square, and adjacent semicircles are tangent to each other. A small circle centered at the center of the square is tangent to each of the four semicircles, as shown below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

The diameter of the small circle can be written as \((\sqrt{a} + b)(\sqrt{c} + d),\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are integers. What is \(a + b + c + d?\)

Square \(ABCD\) has sides of length \(4.\) Points \(P\) and \(Q\) lie on \(\overline{AD}\) and \(\overline{CD},\) respectively, with \(AP = \tfrac{8}{5}\) and \(DQ = \tfrac{10}{3}.\) A path begins along the line segment from \(P\) to \(Q\) and continues by reflecting against the sides of \(ABCD\) (with congruent incoming and outgoing angles), as shown in the figure. If the path hits a vertex of the square, then it terminates there; otherwise it continues forever.

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

At which vertex does the path terminate?

In the figure below, the outside square contains infinitely many squares, each of them with the same center and sides parallel to the outside square. The ratio of the side length of each inner square to that of the next outer square is \(k,\) where \(0 \lt k \lt 1.\) The spaces between squares are alternately shaded, as shown in the figure (which is not necessarily drawn to scale).

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

The area of the shaded portion of the figure is \(64\%\) of the area of the original square. What is \(k?\)

In the figure shown below, major arc \(AD\) and minor arc \(BC\) have the same center, \(O.\) Also, \(A\) lies between \(O\) and \(B,\) and \(D\) lies between \(O\) and \(C.\) Major arc \(AD,\) minor arc \(BC,\) and each of the two segments \(AB\) and \(CD\) have length \(2\pi.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

What is the distance from \(O\) to \(A?\)

Points \(F,\) \(G,\) and \(H\) are collinear with \(G\) between \(F\) and \(H.\) The ellipse with foci at \(G\) and \(H\) is internally tangent to the ellipse with foci at \(F\) and \(G,\) as shown below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

The two ellipses have the same eccentricity \(e,\) and the ratio of their areas is \(2025.\) (Recall that the eccentricity of an ellipse is \(e = \dfrac{c}{a},\) where \(c\) is the distance from the center to a focus, and \(2a\) is the length of the major axis.) What is \(e?\)

The base of the pentahedron shown below is a \(13 \times 8\) rectangle, and its lateral faces are two isosceles triangles with base of length \(8\) and congruent sides of length \(13,\) and two isosceles trapezoids with bases of lengths \(7\) and \(13\) and nonparallel sides of length \(13.\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

What is the volume of the pentahedron?

A circle of radius \(r\) is surrounded by \(12\) circles of radius \(1,\) externally tangent to the central circle and sequentially tangent to each other, as shown. Then \(r\) can be written as \(\sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b} + c,\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c\) are integers. What is \(a + b + c?\)

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

The windshield wiper on the driver’s side of a large bus is depicted below.

[Figure 1](attached-image-8)

Arm \(\overline{AB}\) pivots back and forth around point \(A,\) sweeping out an arc of \(60^\circ,\) symmetric about the vertical line through \(A.\) The wiper blade \(\overline{CD}\) is attached to \(B\) at its midpoint and stays vertical as the arm moves. The arm is \(3\) feet long, and the wiper blade is \(3.5\) feet tall. What is the area of the windshield cleaned by the wiper, in square feet, to the nearest hundredth? (Assume that the windshield is a flat vertical surface.)

mappings.rationale: External tangency makes adjacent semicircle-center distances equal twice their radius. Their centers form a square, whose circumradius equals the sum of a semicircle radius and the small-circle radius.

mappings.answerReason: Set A=(0,0), B=(4,0), D=(0,4). The unfolded ray is y=8/5+(18/25)x. At a grid corner (4m,4n), 25n=18m+10, so m≡5 modulo 25. The first forward corner has m=5 and n=4, namely (20,16). Odd horizontal and even vertical tile indices fold to B.

mappings.answerReason: Normalize the outside area to 1. Since 0<k<1, the shaded area is (1-k²)(1+k⁴+k⁸+...)=1/(1+k²). Setting this equal to 16/25 gives k²=9/16, hence k=3/4. Equivalently, the unshaded area equals k² times the shaded area.

mappings.answerReason: Let r=OA and let θ be the minor central angle in radians. Then r(2π-θ)=2π and (r+2π)θ=2π. Thus 1/r+1/(r+2π)=1, giving r²+(2π-2)r-2π=0. Completing the square yields (r+π-1)²=1+π²; the positive radius is 1-π+√(1+π²).
